messages:
Anya: Quick sync — we need to lock scope for the model-catalog onboarding playbook for vertical customers (fin / health). Sales is asking for per-customer benchmark runs. Proposal: keep a lean default onboarding and offer a paid "vertical benchmark" add-on. thoughts?

Rob: agree on tiering. default should be lightweight smoke tests + perf profile. keep the heavy runs opt-in.

Sam: +1. also want to call out rollout criteria for new model versions: must pass perf smoke, stability (no >1% regression on eval set), and memory KV behavior check.

Jordan (sales): customers are pushing for guarantees during migration windows. they want SLA-style commitments if we run their benchmark. can we map add-on to a clear SLO?

Lina: if it's paid, we can include a 4-week migration runway: 2 weeks for benchmark + tuning, 2 weeks for canary. customers get a one-time compatibility report and recommended pin/roll policy.

Anya: rough launch criteria I'm thinking:
- default catalog onboarding: docs + automated smoke (no SLAs)
- vertical benchmark add-on (paid): defined metrics, migration runway, optional pin support + rollback plan
- internal OWNER approves model for catalog (product + ml + eng)

Sam: benchmark metrics suggestion block:
```
metrics:
  - latency_p50_ms: <200
  - latency_p95_ms: <400
  - accuracy_delta_pct: <3 (vs baseline)
  - token_cost_per_1k: <0.45 USD
  - stability_errors_per_1k_requests: <0.5
```
Those thresholds are placeholders — we should param by hardware bucket.

Rob: operational constraints: vertical runs will need dedicated capacity reservations for the window or a guaranteed Dedicated slot. if customers expect tight p95, recommend Dedicated or pinned model variants.

Jordan (sales): ok that's helpful. for enterprise deals we can carve the benchmark + migration runway into contract. but need clear docs on what we will and will not remediate (e.g., we won't retrain models).

Lina: suggestion on pin policy for migrations:
- if customer opts-in to pinned model, allow 90-day pin with automatic alerting at 60/30/10 days;
- migrations after pin expire require a documented canary (5% -> 20% -> 100%) and rollback plan.

Anya: decision items we should resolve in this thread before go/no-go for Q2 pilot:
1) exact metric set & thresholds (Sam to propose)
2) pricing model for vertical benchmark add-on (Revenue required)
3) ops runbook for migration runway (Rob + Lina)
4) customer-facing doc template + legal checklist (Jordan)

ops-bot: Reminder: create ticket in PLAT-ops backlog for capacity reservations if add-on is approved.

Sam: I'll draft metric ranges and hardware-bucket mapping by EOW.

Rob: I'll prototype a canary schedule template and minimal runbook.

Jordan (sales): I'll gather 3 customer asks (fin, health, retail) and outline contract language options.

Lina: I'll draft the customer deliverable (compatibility report template).

Anya: sweet — we'll reconvene next Tue 11a to sign off on pilot scope. tagging @here so product/solutions/sales/ops know we're locking scope soon :thumbsup: 

Jordan (sales): noted. thanks all.

Anya: one last note — prefer we keep the default catalog onboarding timeline to <72h from submission to smoke results to avoid blocking self-serve users. heavier runs can be scheduled with SLA windows.

Rob: agree. keep self-serve fast. paid add-on is the right lever.

ops-bot: Ticket created: PLAT-ops-4521 (capacity reservation template)
